findings: University College Utrecht, part of Utrecht University, offers an interdisciplinary English-taught Liberal Arts and Sciences degree. The generic normalized programme leaves the degree award and discipline unspecified. An interdomain Humanities and Social Sciences BA is a formally available representative example based on the programme’s examples of linking disciplines in the study of culture and society. It is one of several structures and is selected independently of UCR fit. The credit map uses the 75 EC major minimum including a 15 EC thesis, the semester-one 7.5 EC Academic Core, one 7.5 EC qualifying Language and Culture course, 30 EC of nonoverlapping methodology and 60 EC of further choice. Article 3.6 requires each domain’s methods before the thesis even if it is written in one domain, and permits fewer courses when choices overlap. Introductory Humanities and Social Sciences methods are UCACCMET13 and UCACCMET12 respectively; each domain has a minimum 7.5 EC at level 2. Language and methodology required for the degree or major are excluded from the 75 EC minimum.

Students complete 30 EC each semester, with Research in Context in semester one and one eligible course from each of the three domains during the first year. Science breadth is within the further choices and the humanities and social-science breadth can come from major courses. Language and Culture is due by semester four and cannot meet breadth. By midterm of semester three students declare the major. The major contains at least two disciplinary tracks from first-level work through UCU advanced finishers, plus the final-year thesis. The degree requires at least 45 EC at level 3, including at least 30 EC within the major. At the minimum major allocation the two 7.5 EC advanced finishers and the 15 EC thesis count toward the degree total and a further 15 EC of level 3 work is needed. Students finish the applicable level 2 methods before thesis. The official guides identify distinct options including formal logic for relevant Humanities disciplines and qualitative inquiry or multivariate statistics for eligible Social Sciences disciplines. The credit map leaves the track, method and approved elective choices open.

Society, culture and science uses economics, politics, sociology, history and documentary to examine institutions and representation, and ecology, governance and health psychology to add environmental and behavioural perspectives. Philosophy contributes normative reasoning and theories of emotion; qualitative methods and statistics offer complementary evidence skills. The power and culture alternative studies authority, inequality and identity via law, comparative politics, conflict, history, art, literature, sociology and media. Climate communication contributes analysis of how public arguments are constructed, not natural science. The life, mind and health alternative builds on cells and molecular processes, physiology, neurobiology and brain and behaviour, progressing to laboratory work, perception, epidemiology, pharmacology, clinical psychology, disease mechanisms and research synthesis. Description-only Psycholinguistics and Perception & Action support cognitive and language breadth. Writing Art’s Histories and Researching the American Century likewise supply substantive humanities inquiry on their descriptions. Psycholinguistics is offered only in spring 2027, so it follows the first-term Brain & Behavior gateway in that term. The resulting schedule uses psychopathology before psychodiagnostics and cell biology before molecular pathology. Pairwise course differences verify distinctness. The environment direction is credible but has substantial coverage in the broad option; the separate economics and quantitative science directions have generator support and remain outside the three-option ceiling. Several Humanities topics are represented through adjacent forms of cultural analysis, without implying a dedicated China Studies, performance or religious studies sequence. The Academic Core and PPD share research and argumentation work. Research in Practice and Research Methods & Statistics share empirical design and statistical analysis. Qualitative Research Methodology matches one permitted Social Sciences methods direction. Historical research and meta-analysis remain separate from the named Humanities methods requirement and the UCU thesis. The optional 15 EC UCR row is comparison-only.
